design_doc.context_problem: Build the Copilot AI PIN — a wearable AI assistant that clips onto clothing, captures ambient audio/video via a Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W module, runs on-device wake-word detection, and offloads all heavy inference to a companion iPhone app over Bluetooth LE. Smart glasses (Ray-Ban Meta or generic BLE) provide an optional overlay display and camera input for visual question answering.
design_doc.requirements_constraints: On-device: wake-word detection (Porcupine) must run offline on Pi Zero. BLE audio streaming must stay under 200 ms latency; Opus codec may be required. iPhone app must handle BLE GATT, Whisper transcription, GPT-4o/4V queries, and iCloud sync. Smart glasses SDK is early-access and may break. Battery life target is 4 hours on Pi Zero. Apple MFi/BLE accessory guidelines constrain certain GATT profiles. API keys for OpenAI must be managed securely by the backend relay.
design_doc.proposed_architecture: Three-tier system: (1) PIN hardware (Pi Zero 2 W) — captures audio/video, runs Porcupine wake-word, streams audio chunks over BLE GATT to iPhone. (2) iPhone companion app (Swift/SwiftUI) — CoreBluetooth GATT client, sends audio to Whisper API, queries GPT-4o, pushes text response back over BLE; syncs to iCloud via Core Data. (3) Backend relay (FastAPI/Python, Priya) — manages API keys and acts as proxy to OpenAI to avoid key exposure on device. Glasses integration is an optional BLE sidecar on the iPhone app.
design_doc.alternatives: Alternative LLM path: run a local llama.cpp model on-device for offline fallback, though Pi Zero compute is likely insufficient. Alternative display: small e-ink screen on the PIN instead of glasses overlay. Alternative speech: on-device Whisper Tiny for lower latency but reduced accuracy. Alternative wake-word: custom TensorFlow Lite model instead of Porcupine to avoid licensing costs.
design_doc.decisions: BLE stack: CoreBluetooth on iOS, BlueZ on Pi. Wake-word: Porcupine (on Pi, no cloud). STT: OpenAI Whisper API (iPhone side). LLM: GPT-4o for Q&A, GPT-4V when image attached. TTS: iOS AVSpeechSynthesizer for earpiece, future HW speaker. Local storage: Core Data + iCloud sync. API key management delegated to FastAPI backend relay.
design_doc.open_questions_risks: 1. Do we need a local fallback LLM (llama.cpp) for offline use? 2. E-ink display on PIN vs. glasses-only for text output. 3. Privacy and data-retention policy for audio clips stored in iCloud. 4. BLE audio latency — Opus codec adoption timeline. 5. Porcupine free-tier keyword limit (one custom keyword); paid GA license budget. 6. Smart glasses SDK stability between firmware updates.

pm_summary.overview: Three-month MVP sprint to ship a wearable AI PIN that offloads intelligence to a paired iPhone. Month 1 delivers the PIN hardware prototype and BLE audio link. Month 2 completes the iPhone companion app and smart glasses passthrough. Month 3 focuses on polish, power optimization, and a TestFlight beta.
pm_summary.scope: Hardware schematic and Pi firmware (Maya), iOS companion app with BLE, Whisper, GPT-4o/4V, and iCloud (Carlos), backend relay for API key management (Priya), smart glasses BLE integration, and full team integration testing by end of Month 2.
pm_summary.implications_for_timeline: BLE audio latency risk could push codec work into Month 2, compressing glasses integration. Porcupine licensing must be resolved before GA release. Smart glasses SDK instability may require a feature flag or graceful degradation path. Power validation on the Pi Zero could extend Month 3 if the 4-hour target is not met.

snippets.title: FastAPI relay: Whisper + GPT-4o proxy (Python)
snippets.purpose: Receive raw audio from the iOS app, forward to OpenAI Whisper for transcription, then query GPT-4o and return the text response — keeping the OpenAI API key server-side.
snippets.code:
import os
from fastapi import FastAPI, UploadFile, HTTPException
from openai import AsyncOpenAI

app = FastAPI()
client = AsyncOpenAI(api_key=os.environ["OPENAI_API_KEY"])

@app.post("/transcribe")
async def transcribe(audio: UploadFile) -> dict:
    audio_bytes = await audio.read()
    transcription = await client.audio.transcriptions.create(
        model="whisper-1",
        file=(audio.filename or "audio.wav", audio_bytes, "audio/wav"),
    )
    return {"text": transcription.text}

@app.post("/query")
async def query(body: dict) -> dict:
    text: str = body.get("text", "")
    image_url: str | None = body.get("image_url")
    if not text:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=422, detail="text is required")
    messages: list = [{"role": "user", "content": []}]
    messages[0]["content"].append({"type": "text", "text": text})
    if image_url:
        messages[0]["content"].append({"type": "image_url", "image_url": {"url": image_url}})
    model = "gpt-4o" if not image_url else "gpt-4-vision-preview"
    response = await client.chat.completions.create(model=model, messages=messages, max_tokens=512)
    return {"answer": response.choices[0].message.content}
snippets.notes: Deploy behind HTTPS with a server-side secret (e.g., `SERVER_API_KEY` pattern from this repo). Rate-limit the /transcribe endpoint per device ID to control OpenAI spend.

snippets.title: Pi Zero 2 W wake-word + BLE audio streamer (Python)
snippets.purpose: Run Porcupine wake-word detection on the Pi Zero, capture audio on detection, and stream raw PCM chunks to the paired iPhone via BlueZ GATT.
snippets.code:
import pvporcupine
import pyaudio
import dbus

ACCESS_KEY = "<PORCUPINE_ACCESS_KEY>"
KEYWORD = "hey copilot"
SAMPLE_RATE = 16_000
FRAME_LENGTH = 512  # Porcupine frame length

porcupine = pvporcupine.create(access_key=ACCESS_KEY, keywords=[KEYWORD])
pa = pyaudio.PyAudio()
stream = pa.open(
    rate=SAMPLE_RATE,
    channels=1,
    format=pyaudio.paInt16,
    input=True,
    frames_per_buffer=FRAME_LENGTH,
)

print("Listening for wake word...")
while True:
    pcm = stream.read(FRAME_LENGTH, exception_on_overflow=False)
    pcm_array = list(int.from_bytes(pcm[i:i+2], 'little', signed=True) for i in range(0, len(pcm), 2))
    result = porcupine.process(pcm_array)
    if result >= 0:
        print("Wake word detected — streaming audio to iPhone")
        # TODO: notify BlueZ GATT characteristic to begin streaming audio chunks
        # gatt_char.WriteValue(pcm, {})
snippets.notes: Replace the dbus stub with a full BlueZ GATT server using the bluezdbus Python library. Evaluate Opus encoding (opuslib) to compress chunks before transmission and reduce BLE payload size.
